program_overview.title: Problem Solving and Computational Thinking
program_overview.tagline: The skill under every other skill: children taught to break problems down, spot patterns and think in steps, six months that change how school feels.
program_overview.description:
Before coding, before advanced maths, before every exam technique, sits one meta-skill: knowing what to do when you do not know what to do. This live online course builds it deliberately in children aged 7 to 12: decomposition (breaking big problems into small ones), pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithmic thinking, the four pillars of computational thinking, trained through puzzles, games, unplugged activities and real-world challenges children genuinely enjoy.

The transfer is the point: the same thinking that cracks a logic puzzle organizes a school project, plans a science experiment and later makes coding feel natural. Parents most often report the change in homework: less "I can’t", more "let me break it down".

Six months at two live classes a week plus two to three hours of playful practice, with two more months in hand when needed. Homework after every class, a mixed challenge every month, and a final exam, a challenge gauntlet plus a friendly viva, that decides the certificate with a free retest. Real thinking, really trained.
what_makes_this_different: The four pillars trained explicitly: decomposition, patterns, abstraction, algorithms, named and practiced
Unplugged first: much of the best thinking training happens away from screens, by design
Transfer is engineered: every skill is bridged to school work out loud
Puzzles children actually like: games, mysteries and build-challenges, not worksheets
An honest 6-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment, gently done: monthly mixed challenges and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What exactly does a problem-solving course teach?
faqs.answer: The four pillars of computational thinking, decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithmic thinking, trained through puzzles, games, unplugged activities and real-world challenges. Children learn named strategies for what to do when stuck, and every skill is deliberately bridged to school work: maths word problems, science projects and even planning homework.

faqs.question: How is this different from a coding course?
faqs.answer: It is the layer underneath coding. Coding courses teach a language; this course teaches the thinking every language assumes, which is why children who take it first find our coding courses dramatically easier. It is equally valuable for children who never code: the same skills power maths, science and exam reasoning.

faqs.question: How long does the course take?
faqs.answer: Six months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of playful practice takes a child from zero to the demo-day capstone in trained thinking. The course keeps two more months in hand for children who need more repetition, no rushing and no penalty.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No, and it is all gentle: classwork in every session, a small homework build after every class, a mixed challenge at the end of every month that revisits earlier skills, and a final exam, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva and short quiz. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Will this help with school and competitive exams?
faqs.answer: Directly: reasoning sections in school assessments, NSO/IMO-style olympiad questions and scholarship tests all draw on exactly these skills, and parents usually notice the homework difference within the first two months, less avoidance, more calm breaking-down of tasks.
